record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Inverse scattering for periodic or quasi-periodic potentials
record.original_question: For a potential whose time dependence is known and is periodic or quasi-periodic, so that Floquet theory converts the problem into a time-independent formulation and scattering can be proved, what is the correct inverse-scattering theory and what data determine the interaction?

evidence.quote: Problem 3- Quasi-Periodic Potential If the time dependence is known, but not linear, then if it is periodic or quasi-periodic, we can turn the problem into a time independent one, using Floquet theory. See e.g. Soffer and Weinstein (1998b). We can prove now the scattering for such problems. How Inverse scattering looks like?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the time-dependent Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$,
$$ i\partial_t \psi(x,t) = \left(-\Delta + V(x,t)\right)\psi(x,t), $$
where the potential $V(x,t)$ depends on time in a known periodic or quasi-periodic way: either $V(x,t+T)=V(x,t)$ for some period $T>0$, or $V(x,t) = W(x,\omega_1 t,\dots,\omega_k t)$ with $W(x,\theta_1,\dots,\theta_k)$ periodic of period $2\pi$ in each $\theta_j$ and frequencies $\omega_1,\dots,\omega_k$ rationally independent. Assume $V$ decays suitably in $x$ so that Floquet theory applies and recasts the dynamics as a time-independent operator $K = -i\partial_\tau - \Delta + V(x,\tau)$ acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d) \otimes L^2(\mathbb{T}^k)$, with respect to which a scattering theory (existence and completeness of the wave operators / scattering operator $S$) holds.

Develop the corresponding inverse scattering theory:

(a) Identify the precise scattering data (e.g., the channel-wise scattering matrix between Floquet/quasi-energy channels, reflection/transmission coefficients indexed by Floquet modes, or fixed-energy scattering amplitudes parametrized by quasi-energies) that should be regarded as the "scattering data" for this time-(quasi-)periodic problem.

(b) Determine which class of such data uniquely determines the spatial profile (and, where applicable, the time profile up to natural symmetries) of $V(x,t)$, and provide a reconstruction procedure recovering $V$ from this data.

State and prove the corresponding uniqueness and reconstruction theorems for inverse scattering with time-periodic and time-quasi-periodic potentials.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search reveals substantial direct scattering and Floquet-theoretic results for time-periodic Schrödinger operators, and inverse scattering transforms for spatially periodic NLS via Riemann-Hilbert methods, but no general inverse scattering theory identifying the data that determine a time-periodic or quasi-periodic potential. The problem is posed as an open question and no resolution was found in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Inverse scattering transform - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The inverse scattering problem is equivalent to a Riemann-Hilbert factorization problem, at least in the case of equations of the line.
status_evidence.claim: Inverse scattering is classically formulated for time-independent or integrable settings, not specifically for general time-(quasi-)periodic potentials.

status_evidence.title: Spectral theory for periodic self-adjoint Dirac operators and inverse scattering transform
status_evidence.snippet: Inverse spectral theory for self-adjoint Dirac operators with periodic potentials is formulated via a Riemann-Hilbert problem approach.
status_evidence.claim: Recent inverse-scattering work addresses spatially periodic potentials via Floquet/Riemann-Hilbert techniques, but the time-periodic inverse problem in the Floquet reduction framework remains unresolved.
